items.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop returns as Canonical’s plan for an immutable default desktop
items.summary: Canonical has restarted development of Ubuntu Core Desktop, an immutable and attestable Ubuntu desktop that will become the default over time. The 2023 developer preview was considered insufficient. All components ship as snaps.

items.title: Windows 11 KB5127936 update released with 41 changes and fixes
items.summary: Microsoft released the KB5127936 preview cumulative update for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, containing 41 changes. Updates include improvements to File Explorer and the Cloud rebuild.

items.title: Attackers turn GitHub issues into supply chain campaign against 61 public repos in less than an hour
items.summary: Attackers leveraged GitHub issue workflows to launch a supply‑chain campaign against 61 public repositories in under an hour. The malicious workflow triggers automatically when a vulnerable action is detected.

items.title: Webinar: How to Build AI Threat Readiness Into Your Security Operations
items.summary: The webinar covers how to embed AI into security operations to shorten the time defenders have to respond. It highlights AI’s role in accelerating threat detection and response.

items.title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
items.summary: A flaw in Telegram for Android allowed attackers to execute code on a victim’s phone when the user answered a voice call. The issue was fixed in version 12.10.4 released in late September.

items.title: The Rise of the Threat Operator: How AI Will Redefine Security Operations and Careers
items.summary: The report explains how AI is automating core SOC tasks such as alert investigation, evidence collection, and response actions. This shift is reshaping security operations roles and organization.

items.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
items.summary: Researcher Ben Zimmermann found 26,400 active cloud and AI credentials in 7.25 million public Gitee repositories. The exposed keys could be used by attackers to access services.

items.title: Online Scam Volumes Double to Overtake Phishing
items.summary: Akamai research indicates online scam detections exceeded six million in Q2 2026, doubling previous volumes and surpassing phishing incidents.

items.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
items.summary: Cisco issued patches for a denial‑of‑service zero‑day in ASA and FTD software that attackers exploit to crash SSL VPN devices remotely.

items.title: Hackers Steal 2.6 Million Records From Sony’s Japanese ISP So-net
items.summary: Hackers exposed 2.6 million records from Sony’s Japanese ISP So‑net, including 54,401 email passwords and 16 bank account records.

items.title: Cisco Patches Actively Exploited ASA and FTD VPN Flaw That Can Crash Firewalls
items.summary: Cisco released patches for the high‑severity CVE‑2026‑76418 vulnerability in ASA and FTD software. The flaw, rated 8.6 on CVSS, could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to crash firewalls. Patches are now available.

items.title: ICO Reprimands Staffordshire Police After Domestic Abuse Breach
items.summary: The UK Information Commissioner’s Office reprimanded Staffordshire Police for a serious breach of personal data. The incident involved the mishandling of domestic abuse victim information. The regulator cited non‑compliance with privacy standards.

items.title: Cisco SD-WAN Zero-Day Exploitation Tied to Volt Typhoon’s ‘Silent Train’ Network
items.summary: Cisco Talos linked a key‑stealing SD‑WAN malware to infrastructure overlapping Volt Typhoon’s Silent Train network. The attack vector exploits Cisco SD‑WAN components. The analysis was published by SecurityWeek.

items.title: GitHub Launches npm Firewall to Block Malicious Packages Before Installation
items.summary: GitHub announced a preview of its npm firewall, designed to block malicious packages during installation. The firewall inspects metadata requests and downloads for malicious activity. It is currently available in public preview for npm only.

items.title: Shadowy AI Relay Disables OpenAI Codex, Claude Code Sandboxes
items.summary: A covert AI relay service supplies OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude code sandboxes to mainland China and other restricted regions. The service disables key security features, exposing users to risk. The relay operates without official authorization.

items.title: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework
items.summary: Cisco Talos identified a new AI‑enabled command‑and‑control framework named NIK C2 circulating in the wild. The framework integrates machine learning for command execution. It represents an emerging threat vector.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Second Cisco Firewall VPN Zero-Day Since August
items.summary: An exploited flaw in Cisco’s Remote Access SSL VPN forces ASA and FTD firewalls to reload, enabling unauthenticated attackers to trigger a reboot. This is the second zero‑day discovered since August. The vulnerability is actively used in the wild.

items.title: NIST Publishes Guidance to Meet Federal Post-Quantum Deadlines
items.summary: NIST released guidance to help federal agencies prioritize post‑quantum cryptography adoption for sensitive systems. The guidance aims to meet the 2031 transition deadline. It outlines a phased implementation roadmap.

items.title: Attacker Tried to Exploit Alpine Linux’s GitLab via CVSS 10.0 Flaw Its Ruby Left Open
items.summary: An attacker attempted to exploit the critical GitLab CVE‑2026‑97229 vulnerability on Alpine Linux’s own GitLab server. The flaw, with a CVSS score of 10.0, could allow code execution via a crafted CI configuration. No successful exploitation was reported.

items.title: MR ROBOT Malware-as-a-Service Targets Indian Bank Customers
items.summary: MR ROBOT, an Android malware‑as‑a‑service platform, rents banking trojans that steal one‑time passwords and card data. The malware targets customers of Indian banks. It operates by compromising mobile devices.

items.title: Admin dropped the F-bomb in a password to show hackers who was really 1337
items.summary: Admin used profanity in a password to deter hackers, but overall security controls were inadequate.

items.title: HHS Filing Puts iRhythm Data Breach Toll at 8.2 Million
items.summary: iRhythm data breach exposed personal and device information; HHS estimates 8.2 million victims.

items.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
items.summary: Attackers exploited a Cisco SD‑WAN flaw to deploy KeyDrift malware that copies encryption keys; the vulnerability was fixed in February.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑41709 allowed privileged attackers to perform actions without logging; Chinese threat actors used it as a zero‑day.

items.title: Unknown APT uses NetamLoader to attack a Win10 OS customized for governments in Asia
items.summary: Kaspersky identified a targeted campaign using NetamLoader against a government‑specific Windows 10 build in Asia.

items.title: Cyber Vulnerabilities Besiege Italy, Absent Clear Cause
items.summary: Researchers note that Italy’s cyber threat landscape differs markedly from global patterns, with unclear reasons.

items.title: Qualys CISO on what security teams can do as exploit campaigns grow
items.summary: Qualys CISO advises teams to focus on exposure windows, prioritize high‑risk flaws, and build trust amid rising AI‑discovered vulnerabilities.

items.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited VMware ESX Zero-Day to Reduce Audit Trail Visibility
items.summary: CISA added CVE‑2026‑41709 to KEV after CrowdStrike confirmed China‑linked Warp Panda used it to hide activity in VMware ESX.

items.title: IT bosses are confident they’ve found the certificates they don’t know about
items.summary: Survey shows 40 % of senior IT leaders feel prepared for TLS renewals, but only 4 % have fully automated certificate management; 61 % experienced outages.

items.title: Attackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Internet-Exposed Palo Alto Networks Management Interfaces
items.summary: Palo Alto warned that threat actors are exploiting patched PHP2Shell vulnerabilities on publicly exposed management interfaces; active exploitation observed.

items.title: Shame and sleepless nights haunt scam victims long after the money is gone
items.summary: The 2026 ITRC Consumer Impact Report found that scam victims often suffer shame and self‑blame, while identity theft victims spend weeks repairing damage. The study surveyed 1,111 U.S. respondents.

items.title: Stolen staff logins are spreading attacks between K-12 school districts
items.summary: 808 K‑12 districts had staff credentials sold on dark‑web marketplaces, enabling attackers to move between schools. This represents 13% of the 6,116 MS‑ISAC members.

items.title: Officials seize domain of top bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine
items.summary: Authorities seized the domain of Virtualine, a Russian‑speaking bullet‑proof hosting provider that accounted for nearly 20% of illicit inflow tracked by researchers.

items.title: Smashing Security podcast #490: How Jared Kushner’s iPhone was allegedly hacked twice
items.summary: The Smashing Security podcast discussed claims that Jared Kushner’s iPhone was hacked twice by Dutch spies and Russian hackers, highlighting concerns about phone security. It also examined weak security keys used by trusted devices.

items.title: Leak site publishes data on more than 41,000 DHS employees obtained by hacktivists
items.summary:
Leak site publishes data on more than 41,000 DHS employees obtained by hacktivists.
The Department of Peace group shared the data with Swiss hacker/journalist maia arson crimew, and DDoSecrets posted it online.

items.title: Inside KeyDrift: Analyzing historical UAT-11473 activity on Cisco SD-WAN
items.summary:
Talos identified UAT-11473, a sophisticated APT.

items.title: Court strikes down West Virginia law barring disclosure of public officials’ personal data
items.summary:
A federal appellate court struck down West Virginia's law restricting disclosure of public officials’ personal data.
The law, intended to protect police and other officials, was ruled unconstitutional.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Police seize Virtualine bulletproof service tied to ransowmare, cybercrime

Japan Airlines reported a data breach affecting roughly 2,000 customers.

items.title: Lawsuit against Ex-Overstock CEO tied to 2020 election film falls apart over question of ‘actual malice’

items.title: Discord to let search engines index public server messages

items.title: Volt Typhoon Used Covert Silent Train Network in Four Zero-Day Exploitation Campaigns

items.title: European digital rights nonprofit noyb sues Scale AI for ‘invasive’ worker surveillance

items.title: Unwrapping Retail Peak Season Cyber Threats
items.summary: Unit 42 outlines key cyber threats that spike during peak retail season, including ransomware and AI‑driven attacks. The post offers guidance on protecting operations and maintaining customer trust.

items.title: US sanctions Russians, North Koreans for laundering IT worker earnings
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Russian and North Korean nationals accused of laundering earnings from illicit IT workers for the Pyongyang regime.

items.title: GitHub’s npm package firewall can block brand-new versions before they install

items.title: Compromised camera management software gives attackers a way into corporate networks
items.summary: Security research shows attackers used compromised camera management software to breach corporate networks. The specific application remains unidentified and logs are missing, complicating attribution. Incidents occurred in September and October.

items.title: 345,000 email addresses stolen in cyberattack on Germany’s far-right party AfD
items.summary: A cyberattack on Germany’s far‑right party AfD exposed over 345,000 email addresses and messages. The breach was reported to Have I Been Pwned on 27 October and is classified as sensitive.

items.title: Swimlane connects custom detections to AI-led investigation and response
items.summary: Swimlane Turbine now lets teams run custom detection logic and forward alerts to Swimlane AI SOC for investigation. The release adds Model Context Protocol support and a Hero AI agent that builds applications via natural‑language prompts.

items.summary: Energy company Engie notified customers that a supply‑chain incident compromised an undisclosed number of customer data records; details of affected data remain unspecified.

items.summary: InfraTrust warns that attackers exploit vulnerabilities in critical network infrastructure, including PHP2Shell flaws in firewall, VPN, and application delivery controller web interfaces.

items.title: AI 'hacker' finds 4 severe bugs in popular industrial control software in under 4 hours
items.summary:
An AI-powered tester discovered four severe EPICS bugs in industrial control software in under four hours.
The bugs include one critical and three high-severity issues that could disrupt research experiments.

items.title: Prolific Hive and Nefilim ransomware affiliate sentenced to 70 months in prison
items.summary:
Artem Stryzhak was sentenced to 70 months for ransomware attacks on hospitals, government, and law firms from 2018-2021.
His actions impacted multiple sectors over several years.

items.title: CyberStrikeAI Uses 44 AI Agents to Automate Hacking Operations Against Japan Targets
items.summary:
CyberStrikeAI used 44 AI agents to automate hacking against Japanese targets.
The attacks employed AI to drive or assist human operators in compromising server environments.

items.title: Microsoft releases Windows OOB updates to distrust eMudhra certificates
items.summary: Microsoft issued out‑of‑band Windows updates to remove trust in certificates linked to compromised eMudhra CA keys, protecting systems that do not receive automatic trust updates.

items.title: Beware the Slasher: AI Could Kill Off Cybersecurity Pros' Skills
items.summary: Author Nathan Hamiel warns that AI could erode core technical skills of cybersecurity professionals, comparing it to obsolete knowledge such as reading atlases or remembering phone numbers.

items.title: Brotli bug reaches far beyond Node.js (CVE-2026-111497)
items.summary: A remote out‑of‑bounds write flaw in the Brotli compression library (CVE‑2026‑111497) threatens many applications, including Node.js, potentially enabling code execution.

items.title: 'Aokigahara' Stealer Targets 'Developer Keyrings' & AI Assistants
items.summary: The Aokigahara malware steals AI session data, developer keyrings, and business information from compromised endpoints, extending traditional infostealer tactics.

items.title: Cyber Incident Forces UNM Health to Cancel Surgeries, Divert Ambulances
items.summary: A ransomware attack by the BYOD group disrupted UNM Health systems, causing surgery cancellations and ambulance diversions while recovery efforts begin.

items.title: Warp discloses breach exposing AI agent logs, user telemetry data
items.summary: Warp disclosed that a third‑party vendor breach exposed agent decision logs and telemetry data for users of its agentic development environment.

items.title: Day 2 of canceled classes at University of New Mexico after Health Sciences Center cyberattack
items.summary: UNM hospitals resume patient intake after initial ambulance diversion, but recovery continues in phases following the cyberattack.

items.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Exposed AI Reasoning to Researchers
items.summary: Researchers discovered a flaw in OpenAI’s API that leaked hidden reasoning traces, leading to a fix and a $6,000 bug bounty award.

items.title: Tailscale Rushes Patches After Uncoordinated Disclosure of ‘Tailworm’ Flaws
items.summary: Tailscale is issuing patches for SSH vulnerabilities disclosed publicly before fixes were available, addressing the uncoordinated “Tailworm” flaws.

items.title: National cyber director rolls out latest pilot in South Carolina, this time for rural hospitals
items.summary: The national cyber director launched a six‑month pilot in South Carolina to connect rural hospitals with free industry cybersecurity services, following a similar water‑sector initiative.

items.title: Hackers repeatedly breached suppliers holding UK police data, watchdog finds
items.summary: UK police data was breached multiple times this decade through third‑party IT suppliers. The breaches highlight ongoing supplier security weaknesses.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ISC2 Launches Cyber-AI Workforce Coalition to Address the Future of AI Security Jobs
items.summary: ISC2 has launched a vendor‑neutral Cyber‑AI Workforce Coalition to map future AI security careers. The coalition aims to align industry needs with workforce development.

items.title: University of New Mexico hospital diverts ambulances after cyberattack
items.summary: The University of New Mexico hospital diverted ambulances for about two hours after a cyberattack. Outpatient surgeries and appointments were suspended for the rest of the day.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: CISA confirms PHP2Shell under attack as researchers clock successful exploits
items.summary: CISA confirmed that PHP 2Shell vulnerabilities are actively exploited. Researchers reported successful shell exploits against both critical PHP flaws.

items.title: Scalable Vector Grief
items.summary: A researcher tested eight SVG sanitizers and bypassed six. A response header can run JavaScript in Firefox even when the XML body is harmless.

items.title: Hackers bury inboxes in spam then show up on Microsoft Teams posing as IT support
items.summary: Threat actors flood employees’ inboxes with spam and then contact them on Microsoft Teams as fake IT support. Arctic Wolf documented more than 400 such incidents.

items.title: Tailscale warns of SSH flaws allowing root privilege escalation
items.summary: Tailscale identified almost a dozen SSH vulnerabilities that could allow credential theft, server crashes, or root privilege escalation. The team is working to patch them.

items.title: The Huntress Tragic Quadrant: Ranking Threats Hitting Businesses Hardest
items.summary: Huntress Labs released the Tragic Quadrant ranking threats that abuse legitimate IT tools and Microsoft 365 sessions. The report highlights high‑impact attack techniques.

items.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
items.summary: GoAhead’s embedded web server does not enforce certificate revocation, allowing revoked client certificates to authenticate. This flaw also enables session decryption.

items.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
items.summary: Apple backported fixes for CVE‑2026‑86950, an out‑of‑bounds write in CoreGraphics, to older iPhones and iPads. The patch addresses arbitrary code execution from malicious files.

items.title: Malicious apps prey on Russians’ anxiety about fuel prices, drone strikes
items.summary: Cybercriminals embed infostealer malware in fake apps that track gas prices, police activity, and drone strikes, targeting Russian users.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Vendor Key Leak Puts Data of 238,000 Denver Health Plan Members at Risk
items.summary: A leaked SquareML access key could allow unauthorized access to a database containing personal and health information for 238,000 Denver Health Plan members.

items.title: Socure links AI agents to verified people and businesses
items.summary: Socure launched Agent Intelligence to detect AI agents, assess their trustworthiness, and link each agent to the verified person or business that authorized it.

items.title: HPE Patches Dozens of Critical Flaws in Networking Products
items.summary: HPE released patches for eight high‑severity defects that could enable remote code execution or authentication bypass in its networking products.

items.title: Sekoia introduces self-hosted deployment for organizations with strict data controls
items.summary: Sekoia added a self‑hosted deployment option, enabling large organizations and regulated entities to run the SOC platform on their own infrastructure.

items.title: DNSFilter LUMINATE unifies DNS security, AI controls and remote work protection
items.summary: DNSFilter introduced LUMINATE, a platform that consolidates DNS security, AI risk controls, and remote‑work protection into a single agent and console.

items.title: FireMon Agentic AI helps teams investigate access and prepare policy changes
items.summary: FireMon unveiled Agentic AI, allowing network security teams to use AI agents for investigating access and drafting policy changes within their management suite.

items.title: Exeon expands threat detection to shadow AI and autonomous agents
items.summary: Exeon Analytics launched Exeon.AgentGuard to provide visibility into approved and shadow AI usage, autonomous agent activity, and associated data flows.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Teams External Chat to Breach Organizations in Under 15 Minutes
items.summary: Arctic Wolf warned that Microsoft Teams external chat can be exploited for rapid social engineering attacks, enabling breaches in under 15 minutes.

items.title: Microsoft releases out-of-band Windows fixes with certificate updates
items.summary: Microsoft issued out‑of‑band Windows updates that include certificate trust list changes, addressing issues related to eMudhra and other certificate authorities.

items.summary: Managing access to security tools shouldn't require another manual process. As organizations grow, keeping user accounts and permissions up to date becomes…

items.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
items.summary: Microsoft has fixed a flaw in its Authenticator app for Android that let a malicious app with no permissions pose as a trusted Microsoft app, such as Teams, and collect sign-in tokens for a victim's work account.…

items.title: Unexplained DreamHost Incident Prompts Email, FTP Password Resets
items.summary:
The company says it reacted to an issue affecting some of its systems, including DreamHost webmail.
